title: Extending the C++ Execution Control Library to Support Dynamic Parallel Runtime Systems
problem: C++26 execution control library (senders and receivers) provides interface for asynchronous work coordination on heterogeneous backends, but lacks integration with dynamic runtime systems that create work at runtime and expose massive oversubscription.
motivation: Standardized C++ execution control idioms enable structured parallelism and composable heterogeneous programming. However, applicability to dynamic runtimes (e.g., Qthreads) with work discovery at runtime and concurrency vastly exceeding hardware resources remains unexplored. Demonstrating interoperability is crucial for broader adoption.
method: Implement sender-based interface for Qthreads user-level threading library, demonstrating that C++26 execution control patterns (senders/receivers) extend to dynamic runtime systems where work is discovered and created dynamically.
key_novelty: First integration of C++26 execution control library with dynamic parallel runtime system (Qthreads), demonstrating applicability beyond traditional static parallel frameworks.
contributions: Sender-based interface implementation for Qthreads user-level threading
Demonstration of C++26 execution control patterns with dynamic work discovery
Measurement of interoperability layer overhead in fine-grained parallel settings
Identification of additional optimization opportunities through standard interface
limitations: Abstract-only; specific overhead measurements, scalability analysis, and comparison with other runtime integration approaches not provided.
primary_theme: Runtime integration with standardized parallel programming interfaces
